video_title: Why Processes Exist: Isolation Over Speed
core_insight: Processes exist to contain failure and enable independent evolution, not for performance. Isolation forces explicit communication, which trades latency for resilience and independent scaling.

scenes.voice: You want a system that survives failures and scales independently. Why isn't one big process enough?
scenes.visual: Single monolith box with threads inside, one red crack spreads to all parts. Text overlay: one bug, one crash, all down.

scenes.voice: A single process with shared memory means one slow request blocks all threads, one segfault kills everything, and a deploy touches everything.
scenes.visual: Zoom into shared memory space with multiple threads accessing same data, a slow thread blocks others.

scenes.voice: The obvious fix is threads. Cheap calls, fast. But threads share address space, so no failure isolation. One crash takes the whole service down.
scenes.visual: Threads inside one process box, one thread explodes, whole box goes red.

scenes.voice: The constraint is the network. In distributed systems you can't assume reliable delivery, same time, or that a peer is alive. You need a unit that can fail alone.
scenes.visual: Two nodes with dotted unreliable network line between them, clocks showing different times.

scenes.voice: That's the process. An autonomous worker with its own memory, lifecycle, and mailbox. It talks by messages, not shared memory. Like chefs passing plates, not reaching into each other's pans.
scenes.visual: Kitchen brigade analogy: three chefs at separate stations passing plates. Then map to Process A, B, C boxes.

scenes.voice: Isolation gives you containment and independent scale and deploy. The cost is latency. Message passing is orders of magnitude slower than in-process calls.
scenes.visual: Mermaid flowchart showing Process A -> message -> Process B -> message -> Process C with unreliable network dotted lines.
scenes.mermaid:
flowchart LR
    A[Process A\nlocal state] -->|message| B[Process B\nlocal state]
    B -->|message| C[Process C\nlocal state]
    A -. unreliable network .-> B
    B -. unreliable network .-> C

scenes.voice: So choose process boundaries where the network cost is worth the gain in fault isolation, independent lifecycle, and team ownership. Not for code reuse.
scenes.visual: E-commerce flow: API Gateway -> Order Process -> Payment Process -> Inventory Process -> Notification Process, each as separate deployable boxes.

scenes.voice: A process is an isolated unit with local state that communicates explicitly. Design for partial failure, timeouts, and idempotency. You pay latency for resilience.
scenes.visual: Summary card with three bullets: Isolated worker, Message passing only, Fail alone.

mental_model: Think of a process as an autonomous worker with its own memory and mailbox. It does work locally and coordinates by sending messages. The system is independent workers plus an unreliable network. Design boundaries around failure domains and team ownership, not performance.
final_takeaway: Processes exist for independent failure, scaling, and deployment. You trade in-process speed for isolation and resilience.
